story.title: The Freshman Gauntlet: From Overwhelmed to Overcomer
story.text: Stepping onto campus for the first time, a wave of both exhilaration and sheer terror washed over me. The sheer scale of the university, the bustling crowds, the unfamiliar faces – it was a stark contrast to my quiet hometown. My first few weeks were a blur of lectures, awkward introductions, and late-night library sessions fueled by instant coffee. I felt like a tiny fish in an ocean, constantly questioning if I belonged. The real test came with the 'Introduction to Macroeconomics' group project. My team was a mix of brilliant but aloof individuals, and I struggled to contribute, feeling my ideas were inadequate. One evening, after a particularly frustrating meeting where my suggestions were brushed aside, I almost gave up. I called my mom, tears welling up, confessing I wasn't cut out for this. She simply said, 'You're stronger than you think, honey. Just keep trying.' Her words spurred me on. I spent hours researching, not just for the project, but to understand the concepts better. The next meeting, I came prepared, not just with ideas, but with data and a clear presentation. To my surprise, my teammates listened. We debated, refined, and eventually, created a presentation we were all proud of. Presenting it felt like a triumph, not just for the grade, but for my own confidence. That first year taught me resilience, the value of asking for help, and that even in the biggest oceans, a small fish can find its current.
story.tldr: Freshman year started overwhelming and isolating, especially during a tough group project, but I pushed through, found my voice, and learned resilience.
